title: Paystride Payroll-Repaid Loan Desk Guidance on Offer Lapse, Payoff, Charge-off and Repayment Method Changes
content:
**Paystride Payroll-Repaid Loan — status and closure rules.** An offer not accepted within the product's offer period lapses. A loan whose balance reaches zero is paid off, and a final overpayment is refunded within the product's refund period, counted in business days. A loan reaching the tier's charge-off figure of days past due is charged off for its whole remaining balance and reported to the credit bureaus when the product reports payment history to them. A change of repayment method follows the repayment terms of the Paystride Payroll-Repaid Loan.

### The statuses involved

| Starting status | Event | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|
| approved | the offer lapses unaccepted within the offer period | withdrawn |
| repaying | the balance reaches zero | paid off |
| repaying | the loan reaches the charge-off figure of days past due | charged off |

### Days past due

Days past due are the calendar days, at today's date, since the earliest scheduled installment that is not fully paid. An installment that has been partly paid still counts as not fully paid.

### Charge-off figure by tier

| Tier | Days past due at which the loan is charged off |
|---|---|
| Paystride Payroll Loan 500 | 120 |
| Paystride Payroll Loan 1000 | 120 |
| Paystride Payroll Loan 2000 | 120 |
| Paystride Payroll Loan 3000 | 120 |
| Paystride Payroll Loan 4000 | 120 |
| Paystride Payroll Loan 5000 | 120 |

A loan reaching 120 days past due is charged off; at 119 days past due it has not reached the figure. The charge-off takes the whole remaining balance, not part of it.

### Hypothetical cases

- A hypothetical loan's earliest installment not fully paid was scheduled 120 calendar days ago: the loan has reached the figure and is charged off for its whole remaining balance, and, the product reporting payment history to the credit bureaus, it is reported to them.
- A hypothetical loan whose final payment exceeds the remaining balance by $12.40: the balance has reached zero, the loan is paid off, and the overpayment of $12.40 is refunded within the refund period.
- A hypothetical offer that has stayed unaccepted beyond the offer period lapses and the loan is withdrawn.
